claims.text: Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 develops multiple non-eutectic phases during conventional cooling.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 exhibits a complex, multistep crystallization sequence.
A short, rapid reheat just above Tg and below primary-crystallization onset is the proposed intervention.
Ultra-rapid cooling can produce an almost fully amorphous Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 structure.
The reheat dwell should be on the order of seconds to tens of seconds.
Intermediate reheating enhances short-range atomic relaxation in the amorphous alloy.
Short-range atomic relaxation reduces free-volume inhomogeneities.
Reducing free-volume inhomogeneities deactivates potential crystallization-nucleation sites.
Reheating between Tg and crystallization onset supplies enough thermal energy for structural relaxation without enabling substantial crystallite nucleation and growth.
Structural relaxation induced by the reheat stabilizes the amorphous matrix.
The proposed stabilization delays primary crystallization relative to standard slower-cooling and reheating protocols.
The intervention will produce a higher retained amorphous fraction than conventional processing.
The intervention will increase thermal stability relative to conventional processing.
The intervention will delay crystallization onset during subsequent heating.
Conventionally rapid- or slow-cooled samples without intermediate reheating exhibit extensive primary crystallization and low amorphous-fraction retention.
The initial cooling rate must exceed a critical quenching threshold for glass formation.
Reheat temperature must remain between measured Tg and crystallization onset, and the dwell must be short enough to avoid crystallite growth.
